text:
alex_infra: folks — quick idea: instead of static per-key token buckets, what if we tie refill_rate to real-time GPU headroom from the scheduler? basically dynamic refill = base_rate * (available_gpus / total_gpus) :thinking:

maya_sre: interesting. that would make limits degrade gracefully as capacity drops. how do you avoid noisy oscillations if headroom fluctuates fast?

alex_infra: good point. plan is to smooth the signal with an exponential moving average (window ~60s) and cap changes per-second. also keep a small local burst allowance so clients don't see micro-throttles.

sam_platform: we should keep separation between org-level budget and key-level enforcement. orgs get a pool derived from committed capacity + dynamic share; keys within org draw from that pool. owner keys can borrow with preemption rules.

jin_telemetry: we need concrete metrics to drive decisions: headroom_pct, pending_queue_len, avg_wait_ms, rejection_rate. suggest we expose headroom signal as a percentile (p50/p95) to avoid being hijacked by outliers.

nora_ml: curious about fairness. if a small org suddenly uses burst bursts, can they starve others? maybe add a fairshare weight that multiplies refill_rate per org by weight/(sum_weights). also preserve reserved baseline for enterprise customers.

zach_cost: cost perspective: tying limits to capacity will reduce overprovisioning but could increase tail latencies during noisy spikes — need SLO tradeoffs. can we auto-scale GPU pools triggered by sustained headroom < 20% for > 5m? that keeps limits stable.

alex_infra: yes autoscale is part of plan. fallback policy: if autoscale can't react, we fall back to model-quantized variants and then to lower-capacity region. admission steps: 1) try current model on local pool; 2) if no headroom, route to cheaper quantized variant (if acceptable); 3) otherwise apply per-org rate limit.

sam_platform: config proto (draft) — simple YAML for per-org/key rules and capacity link:

```yaml
orgs:
  - id: org_123
    base_rate: 200rps
    weight: 1.2
    reserve: 20rps # guaranteed baseline
keys:
  - id: key_abc
    org_id: org_123
    max_burst_tokens: 500
    min_guarantee: 5rps
capacity_signal:
  source: scheduler_headroom
  smoothing_secs: 60
  max_delta_per_sec: 0.05 # 5% rate change per sec
```

maya_sre: love the config. operational concerns: how do we surface why a request was throttled? need machine-readable reject codes: THROTTLE_ORG_CAPACITY, THROTTLE_KEY_BURST, FALLBACK_ROUTING. include suggested retry-after and current_headroom.

jin_telemetry: +1. telemetry events should include: org_id,key_id,decision(reason),headroom_at_decision,queue_len,used_tokens_after. that'll let us compute per-org lost-serve and tune weights.

nora_ml: we should also run a small simulator to validate fairness. i ran a toy sim yesterday with same algo — attached logs:

```
SIM> t=0s headroom=1.00 orgA_rate=200 orgB_rate=50
SIM> spike at t=30s orgA_load x10 -> headroom drops to 0.3 -> orgA refill reduces to 60rps, orgB stays ~50rps
SIM> autoscale triggered at t=6m -> headroom back to 0.65 -> refill ramped up slowly -> peak rejection rate from 12% -> down to 1.2% after scale
```

zach_cost: that sim looks promising. can we quantify cost of autoscale vs lost-revenue from throttles? ops-fin can make a simple threshold.

alex_infra: next steps: 1) prototype capacity linker in admission controller (go); 2) add headroom exporter in scheduler; 3) small chaos run on staging; 4) gather telem. any objections? :thumbsup:

sam_platform: thumbs up from me. i'll sketch the admission controller PR and include config schema.

maya_sre: i'll own the metrics/alerts: set alert if per-org rejection_rate > 5% for 10m or cluster_headroom < 10% for 5m.

jin_telemetry: i'll add events + dashboards. we should log decisions at info level and sample full traces for replays.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: infra/admission/capacity-linked -> staging: required reviewers @sam_platform,@maya_sre,@alex_infra.

alex_infra: great — i'll open a draft PR today and drop the sim scripts. thanks all.
